defect.summary: Eng's class key joins the pair with U+0000 under a comment that asserts, as fact, "NUL separator: cannot occur inside a JSON-sourced identifier, so the join is unambiguous". IT CAN. `moduleId` and `eventType` are unrestricted strings on MicaLogRecord, JSON admits U+0000 via \u0000, and no validator on the readable-log boundary excludes it — so (moduleId "a", eventType "b\u0000c") and (moduleId "a\u0000b", eventType "c") KEY TO ONE CLASS. ⛔ THE CONSEQUENCE UNDER T11 IS A REFUSAL OF A CHAIN THAT MEETS THE FLOOR: nine records, three genuine classes, three events each, k=3 — Eng counts two, returns CANNOT_ASSESS/INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE, and its own message says "2 distinct class(es)" where there are three. ⚠ AND THE BLAST RADIUS IS WIDER AND OLDER THAN T11: this key labels the LEFT variable of the AMI statistic as well as T11's coverage count (five call sites), so a collapse moved the STRUCTURE reading too, silently, since the S94 baseline of 2026-08-30. T11 did not introduce the defect; it made the defect decide whether Eng reads at all. FIX: delete the private delimiter key and call the SHARED length-prefixed one this repository already ships — `contextTupleKey(entry)` from src/mica/tuple-key.ts. No second encoding is written.
defect.ground: Codex cold read 1 of T11's committed bytes, ARC_MICA-VERIFY_T11-Eng-Coverage-1_20261001, verdict FAIL, findings F1 (the class key collapses distinct legal pairs) and F2 (68 green tests cannot distinguish the granted looser rule from the forbidden stricter one). Both REPRODUCED by the build seat against the committed bytes of f7800c6 on 2026-10-01 19:3xZ, with the nine-record counterexample and with Codex's own mutation. ⚠ AND THE REPAIR WAS ALREADY WRITTEN AND DOCUMENTED IN THIS DIRECTORY, NAMING THIS EXACT FAILURE MODE: tuple-key.ts's own header reads "W and R joined with an ASSUMED-forbidden delimiter. Its safety rests entirely on NUL never appearing inside a component, which is a property of the INPUT, not of the encoding." The F4 repair length-prefixed the parts and migrated narrow-W, narrow-R, narrow-K, narrow-T and gate1-scope. ENG WAS NEVER MIGRATED. The fix pinned five instances and left the generator, and the sixth consumer carried the bug for a month.

arbiter.word: I, the arbiter, grant T13: Eng counts observed event classes by the repository's shared collision-proof tuple key and its private delimiter key is deleted, because a count that can merge two legal classes into one is not a count of classes, and Eng's right to read rests on that count.

conditions: PRE-REGISTRATION, WRITTEN BEFORE ANY CODE AND MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN. The change is: delete `classKey`'s delimiter join and return `contextTupleKey(entry)`, importing it from ../tuple-key. ⛔ NO SECOND ENCODING. The repository has exactly one collision-proof tuple key and the whole point of F4 was that there be one; a T13 that writes its own length-prefixed join, however correct, rebuilds the drift it repairs. If the shared helper is wrong for Eng, that is a finding about the helper and its own act.

⛔ THE OPENS ARE TWO FILES AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED — under the rule Frank accepted 2026-10-01 15:15Z. Population: 43 suites, every *.test.ts under src/mica/**, src/glue/** and src/core-door/**, run with the fix applied and compared against the shipped state 173059c. 40 OF 43 IDENTICAL. The three that move: eng.test.ts 68/0 → 71/0 (the fix and its three new tests); core-door.test.ts 31/0 → 30/1 and glue.test.ts 136/0 → 135/1, BOTH of which are the same thing — the door and glue's door check objecting that src/mica/** has drifted with NO LIVE TICKET, which is precisely what this ticket supplies and what its repin clears. ⚠ THE FROZEN BASELINES DO NOT MOVE, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN HOPED: verdict-logic.test.ts stays at its base 26/2 and substrate-snapshot.test.ts at 47/0, both absent from the moving list. Relabelling classes does not change the PARTITION, so the AMI statistic is unchanged on any data without U+0000 in it — which is all real data on this box. A fourth moving suite is a FAILED ROUND.

THE TWO TESTS CODEX ASKED FOR, AND BOTH ARE ALREADY WRITTEN AND BOTH FAIL WITHOUT THE FIX. ① [T11/F1] the nine-record counterexample verbatim — three genuine classes, three events each, k=3 — asserting it is READ, plus a direct assertion that the two colliding pairs produce DIFFERENT keys so the regression names the mechanism and not only its consequence. ② [T11/F2] k qualifying classes AND one class BELOW k, asserting the read continues. Nothing else in eng.test.ts distinguishes the granted rule from the forbidden one.

⛔ MUTATION IS PART OF THE ACCEPTANCE, BECAUSE A GREEN SUITE IS WHAT FAILED LAST TIME. Both tests were confirmed able to fail, measured 2026-10-01 19:4xZ: restoring the NUL join fails [T11/F1] (71 → 70/1); applying CODEX'S OWN MUTATION — `if (qualifying < k || qualifying !== perClassCounts.size)`, the forbidden stricter rule — fails [T11/F2] (71 → 70/1). ⚠ THAT MUTATION PASSED ALL 68 TESTS OF THE SHIPPED SUITE. The ticket forbade the stricter reading in capitals and the suite could not tell the two apart, which is why mutation is a condition here and not a courtesy.

⛔ WHAT A FAIL LOOKS LIKE, pre-registered: (a) a second tuple encoding is written anywhere; (b) the nine-record counterexample is still refused; (c) Codex's stricter-rule mutation still passes the suite; (d) any frozen scenario moves, in either json — neither file is opened by this ticket and the measurement says neither needs to be; (e) a fourth suite moves; (f) the comment that asserted NUL was safe is DELETED rather than struck — it is the evidence of what was believed, and the board rule is strike, never delete; (g) the door reports drift on any file not in `opens`.

THE OTHER FOUR CALL SITES MOVE WITH IT, AND THEY ARE THE REASON THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE TICKET IN SPIRIT. `classKey` is called at five places in eng/index.ts — the AMI statistic's labels, the per-class diagnostics, the remainder filter, and T11's coverage count. All five change behaviour together because they share the function; none needs editing because they all call it. ⚠ THE CONSEQUENCE WORTH SAYING OUT LOUD: this ticket silently repairs the STRUCTURE statistic as well, for any chain that ever carried U+0000 in an identifier. No such chain is known on this box, and "no such chain is known" is not "no such chain existed" — nothing was checking.

CODEX ACCEPTANCE, THIRD READ ON THIS ROUND: verify at committed bytes that no second encoding exists; that the nine-record counterexample reads; that the stricter-rule mutation now fails; that the frozen baselines did not move; and that the struck NUL comment is still legible in the file rather than removed. ⚠ AND THE NAMED LINE IS OWED IN THE BRIEF THIS TIME — Codex's F3: the brief must carry one explicit `Named line:` sentence with the commit identity and the single claim to be graded, instead of eleven acceptance checks and no stated verdict object.

DIGEST-PROVEN RELAY: the fix, its tests and the repin ship in ONE commit (npx ts-node src/core-door/core-door.ts --propose-repin T13-eng-class-key-collision), LINEAR ON TOP OF 173059c and NEVER an amendment of f7800c6 — the Codex brief named that sha and a reader must be able to find the bytes that were judged. ⚠ `--propose-repin` PRINTS AND DOES NOT WRITE; the merge into core-inventory.json is the seat's hand, and every new entry must carry THIS ticket's sha, asserted and not assumed.
